title: Field-fibre comparison for a descended section component
statement: Let $f:X\to B$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $p:T\to B$ be surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and let $\sigma:T\to X$ satisfy $f\circ\sigma=p$. Put $Y=X\times_B T$, with its section $s=(\sigma,\mathrm{id}_T)$ over $T$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $C\subseteq Y$ be open and suppose its fibre at each $t\in T$ is exactly the connected component containing $s(t)$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open whose inverse image in $Y$ is $C$. For every $t\in T$, put $b=p(t)$ and $K=\kappa(t)$, viewed as an extension of $\kappa(b)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension]. The canonical isomorphism $Y_t\simeq X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ identifies the open $U_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ with the connected component of the $K$-rational point induced by $s$ in $Y_t$. In particular this open is geometrically connected over $K$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. If $X_b$ is geometrically connected over $\kappa(b)$, the same identification gives $U_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K=X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $U_b=X_b$ as open subschemes. No flatness or geometric reducedness hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, final assertion that the descended open has the desired fibres; field-fibre identification and rational-section component argument.

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$, $b=p(t)$ and $K=\kappa(t)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] to $f$ and $p$ to identify $Y_t$ with $X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$, compatibly with both projections. Since $C$ is the inverse-image open of $U$, restricting this identification gives $C_t=U_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$: on both sides a morphism to $Y_t$ factors through the open precisely when its composite to $X$ factors through $U$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. By the hypothesis on $C$, this is the connected component containing the point induced by $s$.

source.place: Tag 02V3, lemma-set-points-where-fibres-lci, proof: fibres of the base change are the base changes of the fibres; restriction to an open by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: Base change the section $s$ along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ to obtain $q:\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y_t$ with structural composite the identity. Its unique point lands in $C_t$ by the component hypothesis, so $q$ factors through that open [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus the connected scheme $C_t$ has a $K$-rational point, still a section of its structure morphism. Apply [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] over $K$: every field extension of $K$ leaves $C_t$ connected. This is geometric connectedness of the open identified in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 04KV, lemma-geometrically-connected-if-connected-and-point, final assertion (connected scheme with a rational point).

proof.text: Now assume $X_b$ geometrically connected. By [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], $X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$, hence $Y_t$, is connected. In a connected space the maximal connected subset containing any given point is the whole space. The component description in Step 1 therefore gives $C_t=Y_t$, and hence $U_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K=X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ as open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 057I, lemma-descent-connected-fibres, proof: components over the distinguished fibre agree, being equal to the whole fibre.

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(b)$ is surjective by [lem-pc-field-extension-surjective]. Its base change $\pi:X_b\times_{\kappa(b)}\operatorname{Spec}K\to X_b$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Step 3 says $\pi^{-1}(U_b)$ is the whole source. For each $x\in X_b$, choose a point above it; it belongs to this inverse image, so $x\in U_b$. Thus $U_b$ has the whole underlying open of $X_b$, and the definition of an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] gives $U_b=X_b$ as open subschemes.

source.place: Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective; applied to the field-extension projection in the final fibre assertion of Tag 057I.
